# Display Processing Method and Apparatus for Electronic Devices

## Field of the Invention

The present invention relates to a display processing method and apparatus for an electronic device. More specifically, the invention pertains to an electronic device equipped with a display that is divided into two distinct regions—a first area and a second area—each having different physical characteristics and processing requirements.

## Display Configuration

The display of the electronic device is structured to accommodate both flat and curved viewing surfaces. The first area comprises a flat portion that is exposed on one surface of the device's housing, providing a conventional planar display region. Extending from this first area is a second area, at least a portion of which is curved. This curved second area seamlessly continues from the flat first area, enabling the display to wrap around or extend along the contours of the device housing.

## Processing Architecture

To manage the complexity of rendering content across both the flat and curved regions, the electronic device incorporates a dual-processor architecture. The device features a first processor and a second processor that are operatively connected to one another. Both processors are further connected to at least one memory, which stores the instructions necessary to coordinate their respective operations.

## Operational Instructions

The at least one memory stores a set of first instructions and a set of second instructions that govern the behavior of each processor.

The first instructions, when executed, direct the first processor to process the data intended for the first area of the display. Once this processing is complete, the first processor provides the processed data to the second processor for further handling.

The second instructions, when executed, direct the second processor to receive and process the data provided by the first processor. Based on this processed data, the second processor generates the appropriate data for display on the curved second area. In this manner, the two processors work in coordination to ensure that content is properly rendered across both the flat first area and the curved second area of the display.

## Summary

Through this division of processing responsibilities between the first and second processors, the invention provides an efficient mechanism for handling the distinct rendering requirements of a display having both flat and curved regions. This architecture enables the electronic device to deliver seamless visual output across the entire display surface while optimizing the allocation of processing tasks between the two processors.

# Display Processing Method and Apparatus for Multi-Area Electronic Device Displays

## Field of the Invention

The present invention relates generally to electronic device displays, and more particularly to a display processing method and apparatus designed to efficiently manage displays that incorporate both flat and curved viewing areas. The invention addresses the growing demand for advanced electronic devices featuring curved-edge screens, which present unique challenges in display data processing and rendering.

## Background

Modern electronic devices increasingly employ sophisticated display technologies that extend beyond traditional flat panels. Displays that curve around the edges of a device offer enhanced aesthetic appeal and expanded functionality, enabling manufacturers to create thinner bezels, additional interactive surfaces, and more immersive visual experiences. However, these curved-edge displays introduce significant complexity in display processing, as the flat and curved regions may require different rendering approaches, data handling techniques, and computational resources.

Conventional single-processor display architectures often struggle to efficiently manage the divergent processing requirements of flat and curved display areas simultaneously. This limitation can result in processing bottlenecks, reduced performance, and constraints on design flexibility.

## Summary of the Invention

This invention presents a display processing method and apparatus for an electronic device that features a display divided into two distinct regions: a flat first area and a partially curved second area. To address the processing challenges inherent in such multi-area displays, the invention utilizes a dual-processor architecture in which processing responsibilities are strategically distributed between two dedicated processors.

Specifically, a first processor is configured to handle the display data associated with the flat area, while a second processor is dedicated to generating the display data for the curved area. The two processors are operatively connected, allowing them to coordinate their operations and exchange information as needed to maintain a cohesive and seamless overall display output.

## Detailed Description

In accordance with the invention, the electronic device includes a display panel comprising a flat first area and a partially curved second area. The first processor and the second processor each work in conjunction with dedicated memory storing instructions that, when executed, cause the respective processors to perform their designated display processing tasks.

The first processor accesses its associated memory instructions to process, format, and prepare the display data for presentation on the flat first area. Simultaneously, the second processor accesses its own memory instructions to generate the display data required for the partially curved second area, accounting for the geometric and visual characteristics unique to the curved region.

By distributing the display processing workload across two operatively connected processors, each supported by dedicated memory instructions, the system achieves efficient parallel processing. This architecture reduces the computational burden that would otherwise fall on a single processor and allows each processor to be optimized for the particular demands of its assigned display area.

The operative connection between the two processors enables synchronization of the display output, ensuring that content spanning both the flat and curved areas is rendered consistently and without perceptible discontinuity. This coordination is essential for maintaining visual coherence across the entire display surface.

## Advantages

The dual-processor approach described herein offers several significant advantages. By dividing display processing tasks between two dedicated processors, the invention enables efficient management of complex multi-area displays that would otherwise strain conventional single-processor systems. This distribution of labor improves overall processing performance and responsiveness.

Furthermore, the architecture provides substantial flexibility for the design and implementation of advanced electronic devices featuring curved-edge screens. Manufacturers can leverage this flexibility to develop innovative display configurations without being constrained by the processing limitations of traditional architectures.

In summary, the present invention provides an effective solution for processing display data across displays that combine flat and curved regions, delivering enhanced performance, improved coordination, and greater design flexibility for next-generation electronic devices.

# The Many Faces of Human Knowledge

**Various** perspectives shape the way we understand the world around us. From the sciences to the arts, from philosophy to everyday experience, knowledge comes to us through countless channels, each offering a unique window into reality. No single viewpoint can capture the full complexity of human understanding, which is precisely why diversity of thought remains so essential.

**According** to many researchers, the strength of any intellectual pursuit lies in its ability to embrace multiple approaches. When scientists study a problem, they often draw upon **various** methods—experimentation, observation, statistical analysis, and theoretical modeling—to arrive at reliable conclusions. This layered approach helps reduce error and reveals patterns that might otherwise remain hidden.

Consider how societies make decisions. **According** to political theorists, healthy communities depend on the free exchange of ideas among people holding **various** beliefs and backgrounds. When diverse voices contribute to a conversation, the resulting decisions tend to be more balanced and better informed. Homogeneous thinking, by contrast, often leads to blind spots and missed opportunities.

The same principle applies to personal growth. **According** to educators, students learn most effectively when exposed to **various** teaching styles, subjects, and cultural viewpoints. Encountering unfamiliar ideas challenges our assumptions and encourages deeper reflection.

Ultimately, **various** streams of thought—when brought together thoughtfully—create a richer and more accurate picture of the world. **According** to this understanding, embracing complexity rather than avoiding it is the surest path toward genuine wisdom.

# Patent Abstract

**Display Processing Method and Apparatus for Electronic Device**

A display processing method and apparatus for an electronic device are disclosed. The electronic device comprises a display that is partitioned into a flat first area and a curved second area, enabling differentiated visual output across distinct display regions. The apparatus includes a first processor and a second processor, together with memory storing a first set of instructions executable by the first processor and a second set of instructions executable by the second processor.

In operation, the first processor executes the first set of instructions to perform display processing associated with the flat first area, while the second processor executes the second set of instructions to perform display processing associated with the curved second area. By distributing display processing tasks between the two processors according to the geometric characteristics of the respective display areas, the invention reduces processing load on any single processor, improves rendering efficiency, and optimizes power consumption. The disclosed method and apparatus thereby enhance display performance and user experience for electronic devices employing displays having both flat and curved regions.

# Abstract

A display processing system and method for rendering content across display areas having different geometric configurations. The system includes a memory storing instructions, a first processor, and a second processor. The instructions, when executed, cause the first processor to process display data corresponding to a flat display area, generating first processed data formatted for planar presentation. The first processor provides the first processed data to the second processor. The second processor receives the first processed data and generates second display data corresponding to a curved display area, applying geometric transformations to adapt the content for non-planar rendering. The transformations may account for curvature parameters, viewing angles, and pixel mapping adjustments to maintain visual consistency across the flat and curved display regions. By distributing processing tasks between the first and second processors, the system enables efficient rendering of unified content spanning heterogeneous display surfaces while reducing computational load on any single processor. The disclosed architecture facilitates seamless visual presentation for devices incorporating both flat and curved display portions, such as foldable, edge-curved, or multi-surface display devices.
